newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Anti-fur protestors march naked into Red Square.
newsitem.headline: Anti-fur protestors march naked into Red Square.

text.p: A group of anti-fur demonstrators marched naked into Red Square on Wednesday to protest against a fur exhibition in the Russian capital.
The three women from the anti-fur organisation People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) chanted: "We'd rather go naked than wear fur", as they entered the square clad only in sheets.

"It's another dying trade the Russians want to get rid of," said one of the activists. But Russia remains one of Europe's leading fur exporters and has a high demand for fur itself during the bitterly cold winter months.
The protesters, including one Russian, were stopped by police and escorted to a car.
PETA's claim to fame centred around a series of posters featuring naked supermodels accompanied by the group's slogan: "I'd rather go naked than wear fur".
